modules.name: Atom Registry
modules.purpose: Administered catalog of every atom: what exists, its state, evaluations, where used, platform and per-tenant enablement.

modules.name: Core Agents and Composed-Agent Review
modules.purpose: Super Admin capability section administering core agents and reviewing tenant-composed agents.

modules.name: Memory Architecture
modules.purpose: Administers per-type retention defaults and bounds, redaction policy, right-to-erasure, index machinery, cross-tenant footprint.

modules.name: Eval Harness
modules.purpose: Runs scenarios and suites, records pass/fail history, provides the gate view and drift canary.
key_functions: run scenario or suite on demand

modules.name: Trace Viewer
modules.purpose: Backend-only at V1; traces complete, immutable and inspectable at Tier 1 through backend tooling.
key_functions: trace inspection (backend tooling only at V1)

modules.name: Agent Configuration in the Studio
modules.purpose: Configures agents through the nine-section screen panel; schedule and recipients for the handoff agent.
roles_allowed: quality engineer under an authoring grant

modules.name: Agent Builder
modules.purpose: Composes additional reasoning agents from enabled capabilities; composes from the registry, never adds to it.
key_functions: status view of every composed agent

modules.name: Agent activity panel
modules.purpose: Shows per-agent live status, plain-language activity log, and honest degradation flags.

modules.name: Coaching Rendering
modules.purpose: Renders the coaching card on the Frontline Worker Application with replay and dismiss.

modules.name: Run Player
modules.purpose: The run-player step surface the coaching card overlays.

modules.name: Content Libraries
modules.purpose: Holds the Coaching Corpus, checklist library, severity mapping and routing templates.
roles_allowed: quality engineer under an authoring grant

modules.name: On-Device Detection and Containment
modules.purpose: On-device deterministic detection, severity classification, Severity 1 hold and local containment checklist launch.

modules.name: Deviation workspace and evidence review
modules.purpose: Shows the deviation brief, evidence and containment progress for Supervisors and Quality Managers.

modules.name: Governance gate queue
modules.purpose: Live queue of pending beyond-policy interventions awaiting a human decision.

modules.name: Alert and escalation feed
modules.purpose: Carries deviations, escalations and repeat-coaching alerts.

modules.name: Execution Summary Review and Distribution
modules.purpose: Reviews and distributes the Execution Summary; carries the manual-entry marker.

modules.name: Audit and Retention
modules.purpose: Holds the tenant's immutable audit log and retention behaviour.

modules.name: Shift handoff panel
modules.purpose: Presents the shift handoff brief for acknowledgement and annotation.

modules.name: Worker Lifecycle and Qualifications
modules.purpose: Authoritative source of qualification records used for readiness cross-reference.

record-affecting authority sits with the Quality Manager

may_not: reassign runs to devices they cannot reach
scope_conditions: the release control is not available to a Supervisor

may: approve Platform Engineer changes under maker-checker
set per-tenant enablement under approval discipline

the root has no override because the one-transaction guarantee is an enforced invariant

read counts and volume on the footprint view
scope_conditions: read-only, reason-required, ticket-linked, time-boxed at a two-hour default, tenant-visible with an End-session control, mirrored to the tenant's audit stream

enable a capability inside the tenant's entitlement set

make an offline device appear remotely controlled

capability scope is the atoms named on the agent record

business_rules.statement: Every functionality specification carries a taxonomy sweep, and every sweep produces one of three verdicts per class: covered by a named contract; structurally impossible for a stated reason; or an open gap with a DEC-* identifier.
Classes that cannot apply are marked with a specific reason, never left blank and never marked "not applicable" without one.
Manual fallback never substitutes for a control: it never replaces a specification gate, an evaluation gate, a qualification decision, an approval, a publication, or a Severity 1 hold.
No manual episode may release a Severity 1 hold, satisfy a qualification, complete an approval, or publish content.
No manual entry saves without all five provenance fields (performed by, performed at, entered by, entered at, approved form reference).
business_rules.enforcement_point: provenance-marked entry form on the Delivery Operations Hub

business_rules.statement: Every manually entered value displays a manual-entry marker in every view and every export.
A rejected manual entry produces a documented gap and deletes nothing.
The Delivery Operations Hub is the single record of truth and every other tenant surface derives its state from it.
The Client Command Center authors nothing and owns no records, so it may only ever display a state, never assert one.
No surface may imply that an offline device received or applied anything.
No two surfaces display contradictory states for the same fact at the same as-of time.
Every derived surface displays its own freshness, not the Hub's.
An action that cannot be audited does not happen; an audit-store outage stops every server-side mutating action for every tenant and every account including the root.
No mitigation weakens tenant isolation, the evaluation gate, the audit guarantee, or Quality-Manager-only release.
No scheduling failure is detectable only by the scheduler itself.
business_rules.enforcement_point: independent detector outside the scheduler process, leadership and lease store

business_rules.statement: Every occurrence records both its due time and its actual execution time.
No irreversible scheduled operation can execute twice, under any failover.
Every timestamp outside the clock-skew threshold routes to human resolution rather than ordering a write.
No human absence produces an automatic decision anywhere on the platform.
Every redundancy claim in this blueprint names the level at which its two paths diverge.
An untested redundancy claim is downgraded to `Single` in the register.

No artificial-intelligence model participates in the evaluation of a specification, timing, sequence or evidence rule, and no code path exists by which a model output can set or alter a severity classification.
Every agent activation record carries a reference to the deterministic trigger that preceded it; an activation with no antecedent trigger is rejected and raised as a platform incident.

Every agent effect on state or on a worker is traceable either to a named pre-authorised policy object approved through the Studio approval chain, or to a named human gate decision in the Client Command Center.
Loss of the entire agentic layer leaves specification gates, severity classification and the Severity 1 hold fully operational on every device, online and offline.

Governance takes one of exactly two forms: a human decision in the Client Command Center surface at runtime, or pre-authorised, Studio-authored policy approved at publication. There is no third branch.

Severity classification produced on-device is never overwritten by any server-side computation; a server-side mirror disagreement raises a reconciliation record and does not change the classification.
The Client Command Center activity log entry names the deterministic trigger before it names the agent.
Reaching the configured maximum replan count escalates to a human and never silently continues or silently stops.
Every atom invocation that could be repeated by a replan is idempotent, or is guarded by a recorded invocation key that prevents a second effect.
The agent delivers only assets present in the tenant's approved corpus and only in a locale in which the asset was authored.
Retrieval applies the metadata filter before semantic ranking, so an asset tagged to one screen classification cannot surface on an unrelated screen.
Nothing is machine-translated at runtime, anywhere.
The agent never places, alters or releases a hold created by the on-device deterministic layer, and never writes a severity value.
Every proposal beyond pre-authorised containment becomes a gate item whose card leads with the scope of impact and which never executes without a human decision.
A gate item that reaches its configured window without a decision re-routes to the next person per the Studio-authored policy and never executes and never expires silently.
Escalation delivery for a deviation succeeds when the agent is entirely unavailable.
The brief carries both the device timestamp and the server-receipt timestamp for a deviation that occurred offline.
Escalation routing names recipient roles, never named individuals.
A readiness statement is derived only from the qualification record and never from inference; an unavailable qualification renders as unavailable, never as qualified.
Every brief carries a data-currency statement naming any device or run whose captures had not arrived at assembly time.
When released, the Vision Reasoning Agent's registration declares no side-effect in the deviation-triggering path and no severity write.
When released, the agent's type determines its governance; a state-changing effect re-types it to action and it inherits action-agent governance.
No user interface anywhere on the platform offers atom creation, and every atom in an environment traces to a migration reference.
No platform artifact, document, or interface text states or implies that an atom is built in under an hour.
business_rules.applies_to: all product corpus and interface strings

business_rules.statement: The Agent Builder can compose only from the registry and offers no path to add to it.
No agent holds a write grant to procedural memory; procedural content changes only through Studio publication.
Profile memory contains aggregates only; a write carrying identifiable per-worker content is rejected.
No query path exists that can return another tenant's memory, including under failover, cache, index, or support-session conditions.
business_rules.enforcement_point: query layer, cache keying, index partitioning

business_rules.statement: Nothing from any store is used as external training data, and no fine-tuning of any model occurs.
A tenant retention value outside the platform bounds is rejected at entry with the bound stated, never accepted and logged.
Model, provider and tool failover never broadens an agent's capability scope, memory grants, tenant scope, or governance binding.
business_rules.enforcement_point: permissions re-read from the agent record

business_rules.statement: The semantic cache is keyed within a single tenant and by content version; no cache entry is reachable across tenants.
No configuration, role, or failure mode causes a gate item to execute without a recorded human decision.
A gate item never transitions to expired; the only terminal states are executed following a decision, declined, or explicitly undecided and aging.
An agent identity is rejected as an approver on every approval service on the platform.
No atom, agent, or composed agent can be enabled while any referenced scenario is pending or failing, for any account including the root.
No interface, application programming interface, configuration file, or database state exists that disables the evaluation gate.
business_rules.enforcement_point: platform invariant, rendered ENFORCED in Settings

business_rules.statement: The on-device severity-classification table is evaluated at every version before it distributes; a version that has not been evaluated cannot distribute.
Harness unavailability blocks enablement and never permits it. Failure to evaluate is failure to enable, never a bypass.
Full traces are retained 24 months; decision records persist for the full term of the operational record they explain.
No tenant surface renders raw reasoning internals, and no tenant-facing control implies they could be granted.
The console offers no ambient browsing of tenant content; every record-level access opens a named, reason-required, audited session mirrored to the tenant.
The on-device deterministic layer is unaffected by any quota state.
Availability is sacrificed to isolation without hesitation, in that order. Isolation is never traded for availability.
No Lane A refinement changes any configured value; a refinement that would is routed to Lane B.
No Lane B proposal is ever auto-approved; every approved proposal carries exactly one human decision.
An undecided proposal never expires; at 30 days a stale flag copies to the Quality Manager's digest.
Structural insight never rides the learning pipeline; it enters the Studio authoring queue as a watch item.
An emergency pause reduces agent activations to zero within the affected scope and leaves every deterministic on-device behaviour operating.
Resume is a separate action with its own approval and its own audit record; no automatic resume exists.
No rollback of any kind removes an audit record, re-bases an in-flight run, or restores a capability that has not passed its evaluation scenarios.
Every ability has a stated manual alternative, so no capability exists that only artificial intelligence can perform.
Archiving or removing an artificial-intelligence output from active use never deletes evidence, audit history, decision records, or the record of what the output did.
Artificial intelligence may never remove or rewrite its own audit history, under any configuration, at any authority level, through any mechanism.
Deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it, and the list of those standards is owed by the client.
A change awaiting approval is visibly pending; nothing applies silently.
The Reviewer must be a different person from the Author, no role performs two stages on one submission, and the Release Authority cannot be bypassed.
Configured values are a floor, not a ceiling: the engineer's value is the starting point the platform reasons from, and the loop refines around it only through the Lane B gate.

Package-borne approved values auto-publish as a patch version and distribute per adoption timing; in-flight runs finish on their pinned content. There is no second approval, no ceremony, no per-job decision.

decisions.question: What happens when a command expires?
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Terminal safe state: no command in flight, issuer notified.

decisions.question: Device lost, stolen or destroyed handling.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Unsynced captures lost; run manually closed.

decisions.question: Device storage full handling.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: No evidence deleted; capture blocked.

decisions.question: Peripheral failure handling.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Step incomplete, work reassignable.

decisions.question: Offline trust window expiry behaviour.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: No new gated work; captures preserved.

decisions.question: Which capture types are compatible for package compatibility judgement?
decisions.adopted_working_position: the seven launch capture types of the §5.5.3 set
decisions.status: adopted working position, taken 2026-08-14, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: Compatibility judged against the adopted seven.

decisions.question: Package revoked mid-run: stop or complete-and-flag?
options: stop
complete-and-flag
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Determines whether a run stops or completes flagged on revocation.

decisions.question: Library content changed mid-run interaction with pinned content.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Pinned content in force; interaction undecided.

decisions.question: Severity unclassifiable: resolve upward or stop?
options: resolve upward
stop
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Determines the terminal safe state for unclassifiable severity.

decisions.question: What happens when no eligible recipient is on shift?
decisions.status: Client Decision Required, referenced repeatedly and never resolved
decisions.impact: Default is fallback delivery to the Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback.

decisions.question: What is the out-of-band protocol when both notification channels are down?
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Standing states; safety unaffected; out-of-band contact undefined.

decisions.question: Low-quality agent output handling.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Withheld with a stated reason.

decisions.question: Audit service outage behaviour and messaging.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Server-side writes refuse; recommended message states nothing has been changed.

decisions.question: Regional resilience posture and objectives for the single stated V1 deployment region.
options: (a) accept single-region with multi-zone redundancy and a documented multi-day floor-continuity procedure
(b) warm standby in a second region within the same data-residency boundary
(c) accelerate region-per-tenant from roadmap into V1 for tenants who require it commercially
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation — R&D is option (a) for V1 with option (b) costed and scheduled
decisions.impact: Bounds every recovery objective; 72-hour offline trust-window ceiling is the hard limit.

decisions.question: Device fleet resilience expectations, given the tenant owns the fleet.
options: (a) state no expectation and document the risk at onboarding
(b) publish a recommended spare-device ratio and a maximum recommended offline duration per device
(c) make a minimum standardised device profile a contractual onboarding requirement
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation — R&D is option (b)
decisions.impact: Addresses the platform's only irrecoverable data-loss scenario.

decisions.question: Should the platform contract a second email vendor?
options: (a) keep one vendor
(b) contract a warm secondary for failover
(c) split traffic by criticality, sending safety escalations through a second vendor
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation — R&D is option (b)
decisions.impact: Removes the platform's most likely external single point of failure.

decisions.question: Does one immutable log per tenant permit synchronous replicas of that log?
options: (a) read the rule semantically and permit synchronous replicas of the one log
(b) read it physically and accept a single store
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation — R&D is option (a)
decisions.impact: Determines whether hot-standby audit replication is permitted.

decisions.question: Operational knowledge custody and rehearsal cadence.
options: (a) runbook per contract with a fixed rehearsal cadence
(b) runbooks for the highest-criticality contracts only
(c) rely on engineering knowledge
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation — R&D is (a) for safety- and quality-critical contracts, (b) for advisory ones, never (c)
decisions.impact: Every recovery objective in Chapters 38 and 39 is only as real as the rehearsed procedure behind it.

decisions.question: What are the recovery objectives for every register entry?
decisions.status: Client Decision Required — every objective is open
decisions.impact: Zero register entries have an agreed recovery objective.

decisions.question: Root Super Admin continuity: dual-controlled re-provisioning procedure.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required — the most consequential open item in Chapter 39
decisions.impact: Until decided, the platform's highest authority is a single-person dependency with no documented continuity.

decisions.question: May existing federated users be issued a platform-managed credential during an identity-provider outage?
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Determines outage-time staff access for a fully federated tenant.

decisions.question: The approved-form set, its custody, and approval-window expectations.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required — remains open
decisions.impact: Governs manual fallback forms and Release Authority approval windows.

decisions.question: Archive retrieval expectation.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Bounds object-storage recovery expectations.

decisions.question: Are missed agent activations replayed on recovery after an agentic-layer outage?
options: (a) replay every missed activation on restoration, marked `late_agent_activation`
(b) replay only deviation-class activations and never coaching
(c) replay nothing and record an explicit gap marker on each affected record
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (b)
decisions.impact: Determines whether a deviation during an outage ever receives a brief.

decisions.question: Tenant notification after a platform-side agentic defect.
options: (a) notify every affected tenant with the affected record list
(b) notify only where a record's disposition could have differed
(c) record internally and disclose on request
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (a)
decisions.impact: Quality tenants must know when a control they relied on was not functioning.

decisions.question: Orchestration bound values: max plan steps, max replans, loop timeout, per-tenant concurrency, tool-call budget, reflection cadence, kill-switch threshold.
options: (a) fix all seven platform-wide as engineering-class settings
(b) fix a platform ceiling and let each tenant set stricter values within it
(c) set them per agent type
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (c) layered inside option (b)
decisions.impact: Determines worst-case brief latency, cost per activation, and when a stuck agent becomes a human's problem.

decisions.question: Runaway-loop kill switch: scope, threshold, initiating authority, approval class, and relationship to the emergency pause.
options: (a) strictly per-run and automatic, tripping on the configured loop bound
(b) per-agent and human-pullable at engineering class, with emergency pause reserved for tenant-wide/platform-wide at critical class
(c) collapse the two into one control at critical class
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (a) plus option (b) together
decisions.impact: Determines which control an operator reaches for at 02:00 and whether the root must be woken.

decisions.question: Who may initiate an emergency pause, and what happens when the root is unavailable?
options: (a) Platform Engineer or Admin initiates immediately, root approval required within a window to sustain, automatic resume if not
(b) immediate initiation by an Admin with root approval required to resume
(c) strict root-only initiation with a documented escalation path
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (b)
decisions.impact: Stopping must be fast; restarting must be governed.

decisions.question: Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective for the agentic layer.
options: (a) one objective pair for the whole agentic layer
(b) per-agent objective pairs, tightest for the Deviation and Containment Agent, loosest for the Shift Handoff Agent
(c) per-artifact Recovery Point Objectives with a single Recovery Time Objective for availability
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is (b) combined with (c). No value is proposed; inventing one would be a defect.
decisions.impact: No agentic RTO/RPO is stated anywhere in the Statement of Work.

decisions.question: Prevention Agent behaviour on an offline device when the timing threshold is crossed.
options: (a) deliver the packaged curated default locally, marked as the default
(b) deliver nothing offline and queue the signal
(c) package a small ranked set per screen and select locally by a deterministic rule
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (a)
decisions.impact: A plant with poor coverage would receive no coaching at all under option (b).

decisions.question: Action-agent gating: pre-authorised policy or a per-event human gate?
options: (a) Adopt Reading A and amend §8.3.2, relabelling the Prevention Agent "action, policy-governed"
(b) Adopt Reading B literally and re-type the Prevention Agent's delivery step as non-state-changing
(c) Introduce a third governance class, "pre-authorised action", with its own roster column
decisions.adopted_working_position: Gating is declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field, with values `authoring-time policy`, `runtime human gate`, and `none — reasoning agent`. Prevention Agent = `authoring-time policy`; Deviation and Containment Agent = `runtime human gate` for beyond-policy proposals; Shift Handoff Agent = `none — reasoning agent`; tenant-composed agents = same as reasoning.
decisions.status: adopted working position 2026-08-14, both source readings preserved; Recommendation is option (a)
decisions.impact: If the client rules every action agent must be gated at runtime, real-time coaching cannot ship in its current form.

decisions.question: Who launches the containment checklist — the device or the Deviation and Containment Agent?
options: Option A: the device launches locally from the pinned work package at classification, agent enriches afterwards
the agent launches it (§5.2.2, §5.7.1 reading)
decisions.adopted_working_position: Option A: the device launches the pre-authorised containment checklist locally, from the version-pinned work package, at the instant of classification, with no network required; the agent never triggers the checklist.
decisions.status: adopted working position, taken 2026-08-14 because it is the safer reading; source disagreement stays recorded at section 51.11A
decisions.impact: The agent never triggers the checklist; §5.2.2's "launches" describes the server-side mirror.

decisions.question: The Vision Reasoning Agent's scope, trigger, inputs, outputs, release identity and tier availability.
options: (a) post-hoc descriptive only — annotates evidence, never triggers anything
(b) descriptive plus proposal — raises a governance gate item, which makes it an action agent
(c) deterministic visual gate authored in the Studio, which is not an agent at all
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (a) for the first vision release, with option (c) pursued separately
decisions.impact: Vision is the capability most likely to be over-promised; scope must be written before it is sold.

decisions.question: Is an enabled atom whose evaluations begin failing automatically disabled, or merely flagged?
options: (a) flag only, with a named owner required to decide within a stated window
(b) automatic disablement on any scenario regression
(c) automatic disablement only for effect-class and detection-class atoms, flag-only for read and retrieval atoms
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (c)
decisions.impact: The source commits to flagging immediately but not to disabling.

decisions.question: Model and provider selection for the primary, fallback and lightweight router roles.
options: (a) a single provider for all three roles
(b) two providers split across primary and fallback
(c) a provider-abstracted layer with at least two certified providers per role and a documented substitution procedure
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (b) as the V1 posture, moving to (c)
decisions.impact: Sets unit cost, latency, data-residency posture; a fallback sharing the primary's failure domain is not a fallback.

decisions.question: Prompt governance: authorship, versioning, approval class and trace visibility.
options: (a) prompts are engineering-class settings following Platform Engineer to Admin maker-checker, re-evaluated on change
(b) prompts are critical-class requiring root approval
(c) prompts are versioned artifacts bound to an agent record version
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (c)
decisions.impact: If a prompt can change without re-evaluation, the evaluation gate is decorative.

decisions.question: Semantic cache scope and invalidation.
options: (a) per-tenant cache keyed to include the corpus index version and the pinned workflow version, invalidated on either changing
(b) per-tenant cache with a time bound only
(c) no semantic cache at V1
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (a). Under every option, a cross-tenant cache is prohibited outright and is not a decision.
decisions.impact: A cache outliving a corpus re-index would serve superseded content to a factory floor.

decisions.question: Per-tenant token ceiling and concurrency values, and the behaviour at the ceiling.
options: (a) hard stop at the ceiling — agents unavailable, deterministic layer carries the floor
(b) graceful degradation by class — Deviation and Containment Agent continues past the ceiling while coaching and handoff stop
(c) burst above the ceiling with a recorded overage event
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (b) with option (c)'s recorded burst applied only to the deviation path
decisions.impact: Simultaneously a safety posture and a pricing decision.

decisions.question: Drift-canary cadence and the action on a canary failure.
options: (a) daily for all suites
(b) per-class cadence — effect and detection-class atoms daily, read and retrieval atoms weekly
(c) cadence keyed to provider change events plus a periodic floor
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (b) combined with option (c)'s event trigger
decisions.impact: Sets the maximum time a drifted capability can act on a floor undetected.

decisions.question: Who may reverse a Lane A refinement?
options: (a) Quality Manager and above, mirroring Lane B decision authority
(b) Quality Manager and above for case relevance, platform team for retrieval weighting
(c) automatic reversal only, triggered by a measured degradation
decisions.status: Client Decision Required; Recommendation is option (a)
decisions.impact: Lane A is described as reversible but reversibility with no named actor is not operable.

decisions.question: Does an approved Lane B proposal auto-publishing a patch version conflict with the three-stage Author/Reviewer/Release Authority chain?
decisions.status: carried from the canon, both readings preserved, not closed
decisions.impact: The source's reconciliation phrase is "never auto-approved — not never auto-applied".

decisions.question: What is the authoritative field-by-field assignment of package-borne versus server-only values?
decisions.status: Client Decision Required — said to live in the Part VII package contract, which does not enumerate it
decisions.impact: No implementer may assume which side of the package test a given field falls on.

decisions.question: Composed-agent rollback and retirement lifecycle.
decisions.status: Not specified in the Statement of Work; carried to chapter 41 section 41.8
decisions.impact: Rollback of a deployed composed agent is undefined.

decisions.question: Which named compliance standards require deletion?
decisions.status: referenced from the canon and not resolved; the list is owed by the client
decisions.impact: Deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it.

decisions.question: Confirmation of 24-month worker-personal-data anonymisation under the no-purge model.
decisions.status: referenced from the canon and not resolved
decisions.impact: Anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act.

decisions.question: The source's inconsistency about Plant Manager and Quality Director as roles versus personas.
decisions.status: referenced and not resolved
decisions.impact: "plant manager" is a persona here, not a role.

decisions.question: Handling of in-flight and version-pinned work when a feature is disabled.
decisions.status: referenced from the canon and not resolved
decisions.impact: Studio may lose a configuration surface if the capability is disabled.

decisions.question: Reconnection order after an outage.
decisions.adopted_working_position: the three-phase reconnection order of stop-class commands, then the full capture upload, then the enabling classes
decisions.status: adopted working position taken 2026-08-14 under Section 51.0, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: Governs staged reconnection sequencing.

decisions.question: Deployment failure handling.
decisions.status: Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Last known-good version is the terminal safe state.

decisions.question: Standardised device profile owed by the client.
decisions.status: referenced and remains open
decisions.impact: Pairs with DEC-SPOF-002 spare-device guidance.

decisions.question: Export-control constraints bearing on region choice.
decisions.status: referenced, interacts with DEC-SPOF-001
decisions.impact: Constrains acceptable deployment regions.

workflows.name: Capture to record
workflows.trigger: a worker's action becomes an official record in the Delivery Operations Hub

contradictions.description: DEC-GATE-001: Reading A says action agents may be governed by pre-authorised Studio policy; Reading B says every action agent routes through a human gate before any effect.
conflicting_values: SoW Fact — §3.7, §5.2, §6.6.1: the gate exists for proposed interventions beyond pre-authorised policy
SoW Fact — §8.3.2, §8.3.3: action agents change state, and every one routes through a human gate before any effect; the roster labels the Prevention Agent "action, gated"

contradictions.description: DEC-CONTLAUNCH-001: the source disagrees over whether the agent or the device launches the containment checklist.
conflicting_values: §5.2.2 and §5.7.1: the Deviation and Containment Agent launches the configured containment checklist
§3.4 and §7.9.1 layer b: the device launches it locally from the pinned work package at classification

contradictions.description: DEC-LANEB-001: the three-stage approval chain requires explicit human sign-off at each stage, while an approved Lane B proposal auto-publishes a patch version with no second approval.
conflicting_values: SoW Fact — §5.11.1: no Workflow content reaches the frontline without explicit human sign-off at Author, Reviewer and Release Authority
SoW Fact — §5.16.3, §6.7.4: an approved Lane B proposal auto-publishes a patch version with no second approval, no ceremony

contradictions.description: DEC-PKGFIELD-001: the field-by-field package-borne versus server-only assignment is said to live in the Part VII package contract, and Part VII does not enumerate it.
conflicting_values: SoW Fact — §6.7.4 states it is carried in the package contract of Part VII
Part VII does not enumerate it

contradictions.description: DEC-SPOF-004: "one immutable log per tenant" reads either as a semantic guarantee about one audit truth or as a physical statement about one store.
conflicting_values: semantic reading — permits synchronous replicas of the one log
physical reading — accept a single store

contradictions.description: The illustrative atom catalog contains "Initiate Lot Hold" while the source states the Severity 1 lot hold is automatic from the on-device deterministic layer and the agent's containment work follows the hold.
conflicting_values: SoW Fact — §8.2.4: Initiate Lot Hold appears in the illustrative atom catalog
SoW Fact — §8.3.3: the Severity 1 lot hold is automatic and fires from the on-device deterministic layer

contradictions.description: The evaluation seed scenario torque figures are a platform fixture and are not the Bright Bikes specification; the two must not be conflated in any test data set.
conflicting_values: seed scenario: 51 Newton metres against a 47 Newton metre upper specification limit
Bright Bikes: 44 to 47 Newton metres with departures below the lower limit

contradictions.description: DEC-ROLE-001: the source is inconsistent about whether Plant Manager and Quality Director are roles or personas; the Shift Handoff Agent lists "plant manager" as an optional recipient.
conflicting_values: "plant manager" as an optional brief recipient
"plant manager" is a persona here, not a role

contradictions.description: Two distinct stop mechanisms exist in two settings categories at two approval classes, and the source does not state how they relate.
conflicting_values: runaway-loop kill switch — Orchestration setting, engineering class implied
emergency pause — Governance and Safety setting, critical class, root approves

contradictions.description: Emergency pause and resume are critical-class actions the root approves, yet the canon's fallback rules prohibit any fallback depending indefinitely on one person; the source does not state who may initiate a pause.
conflicting_values: pause and resume are critical-class actions that the root approves (§8.8.3)
no fallback may depend indefinitely on one person (canon fallback rules)

contradictions.description: The Prevention Agent's offline behaviour is unstated: the deterministic timing layer runs offline on the device, but retrieval is server-side, so what a worker sees when the threshold is crossed offline is undefined.
conflicting_values: deliver the packaged curated default locally (§5.7.2, §5.14)
deliver nothing offline and queue the timing event as a learning signal

contradictions.description: The source commits to flagging an enabled capability whose evaluations begin failing but does not state whether it is also automatically disabled.
conflicting_values: flagged immediately (§8.5.1)
no stated disablement behaviour

contradictions.description: Two commercially distinct meters exist for the agentic layer and neither substitutes for the other.
conflicting_values: per-tenant token telemetry (inference consumption / cost)
Worker-Shift (commercial usage metric)

controls.label: Approve
controls.effect: Intervention takes effect on approval; audited.

controls.label: Adjust within bounds and approve
controls.effect: Adjusted intervention executes; adjustment is a recorded learning signal.

controls.label: Decline with a categorised reason
controls.effect: Nothing executes; the reason feeds the learning loop.

controls.label: Dismiss
controls.effect: Returns the worker to the step with no state change; recorded as learning and visibility signal.

controls.label: Acknowledge
controls.effect: Command Center action number six; one timestamped state, distinct from resolution.

controls.label: Annotate
controls.effect: Adds a note to the shift handoff brief; recorded.

controls.label: Request an agent re-check
controls.effect: Command Center action number nine; re-runs rule-based evaluation, produces a revision.

controls.label: Manual-close control on the run record
controls.effect: Closes a run for a lost or destroyed device with a mandatory note.

controls.label: End-session
controls.effect: Tenant ends an active support session; mirrored to the tenant audit stream.

controls.label: Enable / Disable (atom)
controls.effect: Submits into the approval cycle; shows pending; never applies silently.

controls.label: Run a scenario or a suite on demand
controls.effect: Executes evaluation scenarios and records pass/fail history.

controls.label: Emergency pause (scope selection, mandatory reason)
allowed_roles: initiation authority open under DEC-PAUSE-001; root approves at critical class
controls.effect: Suspends agent activity per tenant or platform-wide; deterministic layer untouched.

controls.label: Resume
controls.effect: Separate audited critical-class act; no automatic resume exists.

controls.label: Mark a prior case relevant or not relevant
controls.effect: Lane A signal adjusting which prior cases surface next time.

controls.label: Reverse a Lane A refinement
controls.effect: Restores prior ranking behaviour; the reversal is logged.

controls.label: ENFORCED badge on the evaluation gate
allowed_roles: none — it must render as an absence of control, not a disabled control
controls.effect: Shows the gate is locked with no approval path around it.
